spec_match.rationale: The demo rests on `container-type: inline-size style`, which is invalid css-contain-3 grammar — verified via CSS.supports('container-type','inline-size style') === false in this browser — so the whole declaration is dropped, the element is never a size container, and the size branch (Rule A) cannot fire anywhere; the code block also mis-teaches that mixed queries 'need both container-type values'.

interactive.rationale: Width slider, featured toggle, a resizable container and a live truth-table matrix are real controls, even though the underlying CSS is broken.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card's promise (resizable card, custom-property flag, Rule C comma OR, live truth table) matches the page's structure.

edge_cases.rationale: No capability detection at all: in a pre-150 browser Rule C is parser-dropped (and Rule A broken everywhere), yet the matrix and truth table still claim 'size fires'/'both fire' because they are computed from slider state, not from observed styles.

references.rationale: The ChromeStatus link points at feature 5132626887450624, not this folder's identity 6196591858941952 — a wrong-id reference that would mislead the slug self-heal script.

conformance.rationale: The shared suite proves real parse/CSSOM contracts and honestly fails 4 of 5 in this pre-150 browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Verified via headless Chromium 141 cloud fallback (full-page screenshot + DOM + a CSS.supports probe, not chrome-devtools-mcp): page renders with narrow+off matrix state and 1/4/0 conformance panel; slider, toggle and drag-resize were not driven.

telemetry_health.rationale: Baseline injected telemetry only; no interaction/assert events, so the broken size branch would never surface in telemetry.

design_system.rationale: Mostly variables and the toggle/active states override background+color together, but the code sample uses raw `border-color: green` and badge-style pairs --accent-emerald with --text-black (verify AA for small bold text).

accessibility.rationale: Controls are native (buttons, range with aria-label, table with aria-label), but the toggle lacks aria-pressed, matrix state changes are colour/weight-only with no live region, and badge appearance/disappearance is unannounced.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Controls wrap and the matrix collapses to two columns at 600px; clean at 1280px headless, but the wide truth table risks overflow at ≈360px and drag-resize has no touch-friendly alternative beyond the slider (untested here).

openQuestions.title: Remove the invalid `container-type: inline-size style` — it breaks the size branch everywhere
openQuestions.detail: css-contain-3 grammar is `normal | [ size | inline-size ] || scroll-state`; `style` is not a container-type value (every element is a style container automatically). CSS.supports('container-type','inline-size style') is false, so the declaration is dropped, .demo-container is type normal, and `(width > 320px)` never matches in ANY browser — the demo's size axis is dead and the code block teaches readers to write the same broken line. Change to `container-type: inline-size` and delete the 'needs both container-type values' comment.

openQuestions.title: Correct the ChromeStatus reference to feature 6196591858941952
openQuestions.detail: The see-also links chromestatus.com/feature/5132626887450624, but this folder's identity (lineage note, feature index, conformance suite) is 6196591858941952. The embedded id is the self-heal anchor used by the slug-recovery script, so a wrong id is worse than a missing one.

openQuestions.title: Derive the truth-table matrix from observed styles, not slider arithmetic
openQuestions.detail: updateMatrix() computes 'size fires'/'both fire' from `w > 320` in JS, so it reports rules firing even where Rule A is broken and Rule C is parser-dropped (this browser). Read back the observable instead — e.g. getComputedStyle on .card-body display or badge visibility — so the matrix becomes evidence rather than assertion, and pair it with a 'requires Chrome 150+' notice when Rule C is absent from the CSSOM.

openQuestions.title: Track the drag-resize affordance the note advertises
openQuestions.detail: The intro tells users to drag the container's resize handle, but isWide only updates from the slider — dragging changes the real container width while the matrix and readout go stale. Observe the container with ResizeObserver and feed the same state path.

openQuestions.title: Announce state changes and mark toggle state
openQuestions.detail: Add aria-pressed to the Off/On featured buttons and a polite live region summarising which rules currently fire, so the demo's state machine is perceivable non-visually.

summary: Reviewed with the headless-Chromium-141 cloud fallback (not chrome-devtools-mcp): full-page screenshot + DOM of /v149/comma-separated-container-queries/mixed-query-types/, the feature /conformance/ route (HTTP 200; panel 1 pass / 4 fail / 0 blocked), and a targeted CSS.supports probe. The page renders cleanly, but three major defects stand: `container-type: inline-size style` is invalid grammar so the size branch is dead in every browser; the truth-table/matrix report rule firings from slider arithmetic rather than observed styles (false success in unsupported browsers); and the ChromeStatus reference carries the wrong feature id. Slider/toggle/drag interactions were not driven headless.
